chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then slept before entering the state of Ihram. He said: 'He must repeat the ritual bath.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one performs the Ihram bath but sleeps before entering Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the specific condition for the validity of the Ihram bath is clarified: the intention (niyyah) of entering the state of Ihram must accompany the ritual purification. If sleep occurs before this intention is formally made, the prior bath is deemed insufficient for the ritual requirement, necessitating a repeat. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise timing of intention relative to physical acts in ritual jurisprudence.
